text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's commercial banks will raise interest rate on monthly deposits to 20-22 percent from five to six percent from Monday in line with a new record high main rate of 300 percent annually, a bank official said.
-- The British car maker Rover Group hopes to resume car production in Bulgaria from December if the parliament amends the Foreign Investment Law, Bulgarian representatives of the company said.
Rover Group suspended production of Maestro cars in the Black Sea port of Varna in May after it was denied tax benefits.
-- The European Union has so far granted 102.6 million Ecu within its PHARE programme for modernisation of Bulgaria's transportion system, a Transport Ministry official said.
-- Police in Bulgaria's second biggest city of Plovdiv said it has prevented a bank fraud worth 2.5 billion levs.

-- Eighty-two state firms have been excluded from participation in the first voucher privatisation tender among which several plants from Balkankar Holding and the Devnya-based chemical plant Polimeri, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Individuals' deposits in the nine banks put under special supervision by the central bank on Monday will be 100 percent guaranteed by the state, a Bulgarian Socialist Party official told a news conference.

-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutors' Office has launched an investigation against some 30 local bankers over extension of uncollateralised loans, a Chief Prosecutors office official said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 84561
